feedback.reason: The required format and storage combinations cross independently, while session snapshot behavior remains stable. Separating the abstraction from storage implementation avoids a class for every pair.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Export keeps one session snapshot while format and storage are chosen separately.
details.scenarioApplication: Every output format can use either storage provider and observes the same closed-session snapshot.
details.errorCorrection: A class per pair grows with the cross-product even though neither dimension depends on the other.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the storage protocol itself determines the available output format, the two axes are not independent and should not be forced apart.
details.transfer: Separate two axes only when the scenario actually requires their combinations and each can change without redefining the other.

messages.text: A class per pair grows with the cross-product even though neither dimension depends on the other.
Storage should not own CSV/PDF formatting; adding one format would require changes to every store.
The session host would take on output and persistence details that the export abstraction can own.

options.text: Create one exporter class for each format-and-storage pair, such as PdfObjectStoreExporter.
Make every storage backend know how to format CSV and PDF, duplicating export policy in each backend.
Model export format and storage as separate collaborators behind one stable workflow.
Let the session host inspect deployment configuration and write format-specific bytes directly.

prompt: Whiteboard export has two dimensions that change independently: users choose CSV or PDF output, and deployment chooses local or object-store storage. All four combinations are required; closing the board must still observe one stable session snapshot. How should the design represent these choices?

constraints: Preserve the existing caller-facing contract and its stated domain invariant.

feedback.reason: Severity and transport must combine in every pairing, but the deadline contract stays stable. Separate policy from delivery rather than multiplying subclasses or teaching providers domain rules.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Escalation policy decides whether to act; the notifier only delivers the decision.
details.scenarioApplication: The same severity and deadline decision can notify by email, chat, or pager.
details.errorCorrection: A class matrix duplicates the same deadline behavior for every policy/provider pairing.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a severity policy requires a delivery channel that other severities cannot use, that constraint must be modeled as a real compatibility rule.
details.transfer: Use independent collaborators when every policy/transport pairing is legitimate and each dimension has its own change boundary.

messages.text: A class matrix duplicates the same deadline behavior for every policy/provider pairing.
Notifiers would become the owners of severity decisions and diverge as transports are added.
Global mutable selection hides which policy a specific escalation uses and makes behavior depend on ambient state.

options.text: Keep escalation policy and delivery provider as separate collaborators.
Create a subclass for every severity-and-notifier pair and duplicate deadline handling in each subclass.
Put severity policy inside each email, chat, and pager provider so each notifier decides when to escalate.
Make one universal notifier choose severity rules from global mutable state at send time.

prompt: An escalation keeps the same ownership and response-deadline rules. The support organization varies its escalation policy by severity, while delivery varies among email, chat, and paging providers; every policy must work with every delivery provider. Which structure avoids coupling those dimensions?

feedback.reason: Market validation and delivery are independent and all combinations are required. Composition keeps the publication invariant stable while allowing either implementation to vary.

details.errorCorrection: Pair-specific subclasses repeat the same visibility rule as the number of markets or channels grows.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The publication owner must still prevent visibility before validation; the Bridge does not replace that invariant.
details.transfer: Keep a stable operation in the abstraction and pass independent policy and implementation collaborators into it.

messages.text: Pair-specific subclasses repeat the same visibility rule as the number of markets or channels grows.
Moving validation into transports makes correctness depend on which channel happens to be used.
A listing is domain data; it should not choose infrastructure from ambient deployment state.

options.text: Create a distinct listing publisher subclass for every market-and-channel combination.
Place price rules in the API adapter and stock rules in the feed exporter so each channel validates differently.
Let the listing entity choose its own API client or feed file based on the current deployment.
Compose market validation and channel delivery behind the publication workflow.

prompt: Inventory publication has a stable rule: a listing is visible only after price and stock validation. Validation rules vary by market, while delivery varies by API or scheduled feed; each market can publish through either channel. How should those axes be composed?

feedback.reason: Allocation policy and vendor protocol are independent, with an explicit all-combinations requirement. The abstraction preserves the request contract while implementations vary separately.

details.scenarioApplication: Every allocation policy can dispatch through each vendor without changing the request promise.
details.errorCorrection: Cross-product subclasses duplicate stable request handling for combinations that are independently selectable.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a vendor cannot accept the output of a particular allocation policy, that pair is not a valid combination and should be stated.
details.transfer: Use separated variation axes when the legal combinations are explicit and the shared domain promise remains invariant.

messages.text: Cross-product subclasses duplicate stable request handling for combinations that are independently selectable.
Vendor protocols should not redefine the business allocation policy or its promise.
Mixing split decisions and transport calls couples domain data to every provider protocol.

options.text: Create a fulfillment subclass for each allocation-policy/vendor pair and copy request handling into all of them.
Inject vendor transport independently from the fulfillment allocation policy.
Let each vendor API decide how many splits are allowed and what delivery promise they preserve.
Make the request itself call vendor-specific endpoints while it computes the split.

prompt: A backordered request may be split under a business allocation policy, then dispatched using any of three vendor APIs. The split must retain the original request identity and delivery promise; every allocation policy supports every vendor API. Which design handles the crossing choices?

feedback.reason: The case varies approval policy but supplies one shared map implementation and no requirement for their combinations to evolve independently. A second abstraction axis would add indirection without a demonstrated variation.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Add a separate implementation axis if additional map providers later vary independently of approval policy.
details.transfer: Do not introduce a Bridge merely because a class accepts a collaborator; both dimensions need real independent variation.

messages.text: One fixed collaborator does not establish an independent implementation dimension; the Bridge would be speculative.
The extra subclass axis has no distinct map variants to represent and duplicates the transfer flow.
Map representation does not own the approval history that transfer must preserve.

options.text: Create a Bridge between approval policy and map provider even though there is only one provider and no independent change.

Keep approval policy focused; do not add a fixed map axis.

feedback.reason: The scenario says pricing and plan validation change together, and checkout has one fixed implementation. A Bridge would separate axes that do not vary independently.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Revisit the structure if checkout providers become independently selectable across the pricing models.
details.transfer: Coupled rules should remain together until visible facts show that their changes and combinations are independent.

messages.text: The checkout collaborator is fixed, so separating it adds no actual variation point.

options.text: Keep pricing policy and plan validation together; no independent axis exists.
Split checkout protocol from pricing into a Bridge even though checkout does not vary in this case.

prompt: A regional bundle keeps pricing consistent with its plan components. The business supports several pricing models, but all bundles use the same plan graph and checkout protocol; the pricing rules are reviewed together with the plan type and never vary independently. What is the smallest fit?

messages.text: Pair-specific subclasses duplicate the same contract and grow as either axis expands.

messages.text: Pair-specific assets duplicate identity behavior for combinations that are already supported independently.

options.text: Create one asset class per storage-and-encoding pair and duplicate stable-identity handling.
Separate asset behavior from storage and encoding implementations.

feedback.reason: The case defines each territory’s complete rule as one reviewed unit and says territory/expiry do not vary independently. A Bridge would make invalid combinations easy to express.

Separate territory from expiry in a Bridge despite the requirement that each legal rule is revised as one unit.

The legal team supplies one complete policy per territory; each policy’s territory and expiry are revised together, with no shared combinations across territories.
